# Fixed: A fingerprinted file is no longer rejected when AcoustID names a sibling recording of the same song

Part of the [custom Lidarr image](https://github.com/chodeus/Lidarr/tree/custom) (`ghcr.io/chodeus/lidarr:custom`), which merges this branch into `develop`. It is stacked on `feat/metadata-source-ids`, which only compares MusicBrainz ids, and merges after it. Reviewed in [#PR_NUMBER](https://github.com/chodeus/Lidarr/pull/PR_NUMBER).

For a fingerprinted file, `DistanceCalculator.TrackDistance` adds the `recording_id` penalty unless AcoustID names the track's own MusicBrainz recording. Its weight of 10 is the heaviest in a track's distance. MusicBrainz often holds one song as several recordings, one per release, and AcoustID can file the fingerprint under a sibling from another release. A right file without a MusicBrainz recording tag then scores 37.5% against the 60% a new download needs, and the whole album is rejected as "Worst track match".

- The AcoustID lookup asks for `meta=recordings` instead of `meta=recordingids`, which adds each named recording's title and length. `LocalTrack.AcoustIdResults` holds the same ids as before; the titles and lengths go in a new `LocalTrack.AcoustIdRecordings`. On 89 fingerprints, both requests named the same recordings above the score threshold.
- A named recording with the track's title, compared as `track_title` compares it (letters and digits only, ignoring case and accents), and a length within 10 seconds of the track's, the grace `track_length` allows, costs 0.2 instead of the full penalty. A file for which it is the only miss scores 87.5% instead of 37.5%, and an album made only of such files stays under the album threshold. A named recording without a title or a length, a track without a length, and a lookup without titles, such as an identification test case, are penalised as before.
- The track's own recording still costs nothing. So a release holding the recording AcoustID named ranks above one holding a sibling, and two same-titled tracks on one release keep their own files. On a single the gap is one track's worth, so a tag field such as country or label that favours the sibling's release can still decide which edition wins.
- A differently titled recording still counts against the file, so an instrumental or clean cut that AcoustID files under the vocal recording, or a remix filed under the original, keeps the penalty.

Tests: in `TrackDistanceFixture`, a named recording with the track's title, also punctuated differently, and a length up to 10 seconds either side costs 0.2, and the track's own recording nothing; another title, an instrumental label, an empty title, a length 10.5 seconds off either way, no length (also against a 5-second track), a track without a length, no titles at all and two empty titles cost the full penalty. `SiblingRecordingFixture` goes through the real `MapReleaseTracks` and `AlbumReleaseDistance`: two same-titled tracks map to their own recordings, the release holding the named recording ranks first, also for a five-track album against a sibling release in a preferred country, a file named under a sibling stays within the track threshold, and a fifteen-track album of them within the album threshold. In `FingerprintingServiceFixture`, the request asks for `meta=recordings`, and the response's titles and lengths are kept beside the ids through the real JSON parsing, a recording without them is kept with none, and a result below the score threshold is left out. The recorded AcoustID requests in `AcoustidResponses.json` now say `meta=recordings`. Fifteen mutations each fail a test: keeping the full penalty for a sibling, waiving it, a sibling penalty of 0.05 or 0.5, charging the track's own recording, ignoring the title or the length, an 11-second or a strict 10-second tolerance, no check on the track's length or on a missing recording length, asking for `meta=recordingids`, not keeping the titles, keeping recordings below the score threshold, and matching two empty titles.
